steps.text: The first arrow must start at the alkene electron pair and point to H of HBr.
A second arrow must go from the H–Br bond to Br, making bromide.
The favoured intermediate is the secondary carbocation $\mathrm{CH_3CH^+CH_3}$.
A lone pair on bromide attacks the positively charged carbon to form 2-bromopropane.
Neutral reactants form a +1 carbocation and a -1 bromide ion; the total charge remains zero.
